description: MRWA Banner Alert PDF Library — Workplace Safety Incident Alerts

alert_types.red: Red Banner Alert — Serious incident / LTI / Near miss with high potential (preliminary notice)
alert_types.amber: Amber Banner Alert — Significant incident / Near miss (preliminary notice)
alert_types.grey: Grey Banner Alert — Final report with lessons learnt and recommendations
alert_types.archive: Closed/resolved alerts moved here for historical reference

banner_workflow.step_1: Red or Amber Banner issued (preliminary notice) → goes in red/ or amber/
banner_workflow.step_3: Grey Banner issued (final report with lessons learnt) → goes in grey/
banner_workflow.step_4: Linked Red+Grey pair archived together → archive/

documents.original_filename: Grey Banner Alert - Final Notice - 57148 - Shoulder injury resulting in LTI - 4 March 2026.pdf

alert.work_activity: Pull-starting pressure water pump in a gravel pit
alert.injury_type: Right shoulder and neck — popping sound and pain during pull-start
contributing_factors: Pressure water pump transported with fuel line not isolated, causing hydraulic lock
Pressure not released from wand trigger before pull starts, contributing to hydraulic lock
Pull cord on pressure washer pump was short, preventing full arm extension
corrective_actions: Replacement of pressure washer pump pull cord with one of suitable length
Reaffirmed requirement to release pressure with wand trigger before pull cord starts
Reaffirmed to isolate fuel line before transporting

documents.original_filename: Grey Banner Alert - Final Notice - 57539 - Worker tripped over parking bay wheel stop bar - 23 March 2026.pdf

alert.short_description: Worker tripped over parking bay wheel stop bar
alert.work_activity: Preparing to depart office for unexpected delivery of supplies
alert.injury_type: Overstretched left leg after tripping over wheel stop bar, pulled muscle
contributing_factors: No signage specifically identifying tripping hazard from wheel stop bars
Worker was unaware of the hazard when walking back to the office
Worker believed foot had cleared the wheel stop bar — different footwear would not have prevented incident
Worker was requested at short notice to collect and deliver supplies
Colour marking on wheel stop bar had faded, reducing effectiveness
corrective_actions: Revisit Slips, Trips & Falls PowerPoint slides at next Office Toolbox
Review and replace signage and refresh colour markings on all parking bay wheel stop bars
Install clear and visible signage identifying tripping hazard within parking bays
additional_learnings: Workers allocated tasks outside normal activities on short notice must assess hazards and risks before proceeding
Workers attending worksite on network must wear appropriate PPE including compliant footwear and hi-vis unless remaining in vehicle

documents.original_filename: Grey Banner Alert - Final Notice - 56820 - Concrete Saw Strikes Worker in Face - 17 February 2026.pdf

alert.short_description: Quick-Cut Saw Strikes Worker in Face
alert.work_activity: Cutting 450mm RCP to length at Road Train Assembly Area in Northam
alert.injury_type: Laceration from nose to lower lip on right side of face from saw blade contact
contributing_factors: SWMS did not contain information on correct placement of RCP to prevent pinching the blade
Work instruction not updated on site to include hazards and risks of cutting RCP
RCP placed on 100mm of residual sand — flange supported one end, sand the other, creating space under the cut point
Contractor SWMS did not cover placement of RCP on suitable surface or in secure position
Project specific and regional risk register did not contain controls for cutting RCPs at ground level
Prestart meeting form was used for multiple days (11th-17th Feb) instead of one form per day
Project Manager required to take on Supervisor responsibilities due to resourcing issues
corrective_actions: Review and update SWMS relating to RCP cutting using quick-cut saws to ensure material is secured to prevent pipe pinching the blade
Update regional project risk registers to include hazards and controls associated with quick-cut saws and RCP securing methods

documents.original_filename: Red Banner Alert - Preliminary Notice - 57801  - Chain used for recovery of maintenance truck, snaps and recoils, smashing through mesh guard and .pdf

alert.short_description: Chain used for recovery of maintenance truck, snaps and recoils, smashing through mesh guard and windscreen
alert.road: Great Northern Hwy (approx 100km west of Kununurra)
alert.work_activity: Recovery of bogged flocon truck using chain attached to posi-track
alert.injury_type: No injuries — chain struck unoccupied vehicle
key_details: Crew used 10mm chain (lashing chain from posi-track) as recovery gear — no proper recovery equipment available
Chain attached between posi-track (6m away) and bogged flocon truck
Chain failed under load, snapped and recoiled through mesh windscreen guard and windscreen
No workers on foot at time — potential for serious injury or fatality had workers been standing nearby
Recovery abandoned, heavy tow mobilised from Kununurra

documents.original_filename: Red Banner Alert - Preliminary Notice - 57872 - TC sustains shoulder injury slipping on roadside batter - 11 April 2026.pdf

alert.short_description: Traffic Controller sustains shoulder injury slipping on roadside batter
alert.work_activity: Setting up traffic management signage for road widening project
alert.injury_type: Left shoulder — slipped on soft batter, grabbed door and roll bar, felt pain
key_details: TC exited vehicle on passenger side, feet slipped on soft batter at road shoulder
TC grabbed door with right hand and roll bar with left hand to right themself
Pain in left shoulder immediately — completed site set up but unable to continue
X-rays showed no bone damage, ultrasound required for further assessment
TC deemed unfit for work for 2 weeks — LTI

documents.original_filename: Red Banner Alert - Preliminary Notice - 57937 - Truck rollover - 15 April 2026.pdf

alert.work_activity: Spreader truck transporting aggregate and towing float with multi tyre roller to pavement repair location
alert.injury_type: No injuries — driver confirmed no injuries after health check
key_details: Spreader truck westbound on South Coast Hwy with partial aggregate load, towing float with roller
Truck came around corner at ~80km/h on slick/wet surface
Lost traction, truck and trailer slid sideways, truck flipped onto its side
Drug and alcohol testing completed — negative
Driver taken for health check — confirmed no injuries
